findings.issue: showdownOf copies every entry of state.result.showdown. Today hand.ts endRound fills result.showdown with every non-folded seat's hole cards, losers included. Spec section 8 lists mucked cards as hidden data, and the 'only shown hands' guarantee depends on TASK-1.15 later shrinking result.showdown. Until that lands, a losing hand that would be mucked in a real game reaches every later view through earlierShowdowns.
findings.evidence: endRound (hand.ts ~318) builds showdown from all active seats -> showdownOf maps all of them into EarlierShowdown.shown -> playerView passes earlierShowdowns to the policy. Not reachable yet: no production caller of showdownOf or actWith exists in src/ (the session loop and bots come later), and showing all hands at showdown matches the current engine's rules. Defence in depth only.
findings.fix: No change needed in this task. Make sure TASK-1.15 (mucking) changes result.showdown or showdownOf so that only hands actually tabled are listed, and add a test asserting that a mucked losing hand is absent from showdownOf.

findings.issue: earlierShowdowns is passed to every policy by reference (A-3, intentional). The array is readonly only at the type level, so a policy that casts it (or JS code) could push or alter entries, and later seats' views would see that data. This is an integrity issue, not a confidentiality one: the array holds only public shown hands, so no hidden card can leak through it.
findings.evidence: the caller's earlierShowdowns array -> view.earlierShowdowns (same reference) -> a policy casts it and mutates -> the next actWith call gives the same array to another seat. Spec section 8 rules out hostile plug-ins, and TypeScript readonly prevents accidental mutation, so this is not reachable within the threat model.
findings.fix: Optional: have the session owner Object.freeze each EarlierShowdown and the list when appending (O(1) per hand, keeps A-3's cost bound).

summary: No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings. playerView builds every field by name from primitives. Cards are numbers. stakes, board, pots (including eligible), players, actions and legalActions are freshly allocated plain object literals: no getters, functions, prototype tricks or closures that lead back to HandState. deck, burned, result and other seats' holeCards never reach the view, and no replay code exists in HandState. legalActions is [] for any seat that is not to act, and it only carries {seat, type, amount} derived from that seat's own stack and public bets. Error messages from actWith/applyAction contain only seat numbers, go to the engine caller rather than the policy, and the policy is not called on a completed hand. applyAction copies the policy's action into a new ActionRecord field by field, so a policy cannot keep a live reference into the next state. The SPEC-02 property test (rotating all hidden deck indices including burns and undealt cards, with a control swap that must change the view) and the SPEC-04 reference-walk test cover the boundary well. Two MINOR defence-in-depth notes: earlierShowdowns depends on TASK-1.15 for mucking, and earlierShowdowns is a shared mutable reference. No new dependencies, no randomness in the module.
